tvShow.name: The WONDERfools
tvShow.overview: A goofy group of townies stumbles into superpowers and fights rising evil as doomsday panic grows in this wild, turn-of-the-century action comedy.

episodes.name: Every Life Comes With a Surprise Twist
episodes.overview: When news of the apocalypse spreads in Haeseong City, a cash-strapped and terminally ill young woman devises a kidnapping plot with two clumsy sidekicks.

episodes.name: Secrets Are Meant To Be Kept
episodes.overview: Eun Chae-ni and her quirky friends Son Gyeong-hun and Kang Ro-bin are baffled by their sudden abilities. A wary Lee Un-jeong confronts his doubts.

episodes.name: Brutes and Bad Luck Do Come in Droves
episodes.overview: The gang witnesses Un-jeong's superpower in a crisis. While they're thrilled after a daring rescue, Un-jeong senses danger nearby.

episodes.name: Boon the King Duck vs Wunderkinder
episodes.overview: Dr. Ha Won-do returns after 20 years, chasing secrets of the Child of Eternity. Later, the gang faces an attack — still unsure of their powers.

episodes.name: All We Need Is You
episodes.overview: Un-jeong leads a bootcamp for the gang to tap into their abilities. Chae-ni confronts her grandma about the superpower's secret.

episodes.name: All Roads Lead to Chae-ni
episodes.overview: Chae-ni wakes up to danger — but finds a surprise lifeline in her pocket. Un-jeong plans with Gyeong-hun and Ro-bin to rescue Chae-ni.

episodes.name: The Guardians of Haeseong City Part 1
episodes.overview: Un-jeong and the gang fight other superpowered followers, while Dr. Ha's risky plan targets Chae-ni.

episodes.name: The Guardians of Haeseong City Part 2
episodes.overview: New Year's Eve 1999. Three misfits use their abilities to battle superpowered villains in an all-out brawl for Haeseong City.

seasons.name: Limited Series
seasons.overview: Eun Chae-ni is the granddaughter of a wealthy restaurant owner. She is smart, polite, and diligent in everything she does, but because she has a different heart from others, she becomes more stubborn as she grows up, and she lives her life on thin ice that may stop at any time, dreaming of a train trip. Lee Woon-jung is a mysterious civil servant with many secrets and no social skills. He is a lonely person who can hardly be by anyone's side, but he comes to realize the meaning of 'us' after meeting Eun Chae-ni.

reviews.author: mariamdk96
reviews.content: The drama is amazing that after finishing it, I already want more. I need to see Lee Unjeong again. Thank you to the talented actor Cha Eunwoo for bringing this character to life so perfectly.

reviews.author: shabsssskitch
reviews.content: Fully satisfied with this drama. The characters and the actors playing them are all brilliant! I love how they all have chemistry. Can't stop laughing all throughout the series. The way the comedy didn't feel underwhelming or overwhelming at all. Every gag was just right amount, the emotional scenes will really tug your heart, the action scenes are not dragging, the romance is so subtle you'd be asking for more and the ending was so satisfying that leaves you smiling from ear to ear. The easiest 1000/10 out of all the kdramas this year.

reviews.author: FantasticCEW
reviews.content: I enjoyed watching every episode, every secknd. The WONDERfools is an excellent drama, very well made. All the cast members are so good, especially my favorite actor CHA EUN-WOO, he portrayed perfectly Lee Unjeong. Eunwoo so powerful, attractive and charismatic. Everyone should watch the Wonderfools to laugh, see actions and feel each emotion.

reviews.author: chellecew
reviews.content:
This drama has EVERYTHING — heart, mystery, comedy, action, emotion, and characters that completely pull you into their world from the very first episode.

Every episode leaves you wanting more. The chemistry between the cast is electric, the storytelling keeps you hooked, and the balance between humor and emotional depth is done so beautifully. One moment you’re laughing, the next you’re sitting there completely speechless.

And Cha Eunwoo? Absolutely phenomenal. His presence, expressions, charisma, and emotional delivery made this drama unforgettable. He brings so much life and depth to his character that you can’t take your eyes off the screen.

WonderFools isn’t just a drama you watch casually — it’s the kind that fully engrosses you and makes you emotionally invested in every character and every twist. One of the most entertaining and addictive dramas I’ve watched in a long time.

10/10. A masterpiece of fun, emotion, and pure magic.

reviews.author: Strawberry_Matcha
reviews.content:
Rating: 10/10.
The WonderFools is a definitive masterpiece among 2026 Korean dramas. From its meticulous production design to its cinematic visual language, the series exemplifies the highest standards of contemporary television. Every element — direction, cinematography, editing, and an expertly curated original soundtrack — coalesces to create an immersive viewing experience that is as emotionally resonant as it is aesthetically assured.
Central to the series’ success is its exemplary casting. The ensemble performs with coherence and nuance, but it is the main lead who anchors the narrative with an extraordinary combination of technical proficiency and emotive depth. Displaying a commanding screen presence, the lead delivers a performance that is restrained when subtlety is required and searingly powerful in moments of heightened drama. His vocal modulation, controlled physicality, and precise emotional timing convey a fully realized character arc that elevates the series from simply well-made to artistically significant.
Particularly noteworthy is the lead’s capacity for transformation. Across the season, he navigates complex psychological terrain with credibility and honesty, rendering scenes of vulnerability and resolve with equal conviction. This performance reflects sustained professional growth and an evident commitment to craft: careful character work, nuanced interactions with co-stars, and an ability to carry pivotal scenes without resorting to melodrama. Such mastery lends the series its emotional core and sustains audience engagement from episode to episode.
Moreover, the production’s technical strengths — striking composition, disciplined pacing, and a soundtrack that enhances rather than overwhelms — provide an ideal framework for the actors’ work. The result is a cohesive drama that balances spectacle with subtlety, offering both immediate entertainment and lasting dramatic substance.
In sum, The WonderFools is not merely the standout K-drama of 2026 by virtue of its production values; it is distinguished by an outstanding central performance that justifies acclaim. The main lead’s portrayal is a career-defining achievement: assured, transformative, and integral to the series’ artistic triumph.

Cha Eun-woo’s performance in The WonderFools is highly impressive and showcases his strength as a skilled actor. His portrayal reflects remarkable control, depth, and professionalism, further affirming his talent and growing presence in the industry.
